name: Right wing
summary: Right-wing politics is the range of ideologies that regard social stratification and inequality as inevitable, natural or desirable, usually justified by tradition, authority, property, religion or competition, and which tend to resist rapid change. Beyond that shared core its defining sources describe a wide variety of strands that disagree on economics, religion, immigration and the state, so few statements are settled for the label as a whole.
scope: The label 'right-wing' as its defining sources use it: the range of ideologies that treat social stratification and hierarchy as inevitable, natural or desirable, the criterion Bobbio, Giddens and Jost give (the left favours greater equality, the right sees society as inevitably hierarchical), joined in the scholarship to resistance to change. Burke's Reflections (named by the reference sources as a founding text of the right) stands as its primary text. It is a positional label: the economic, social and foreign-policy programmes of particular parties or strands (the 2024 US Republican platform, neoliberal, national-conservative, far-right or monarchist programmes) are other subjects and are not used here.
